title: 5 Ways the Dinosaur World Was Nothing Like Ours
summary:
Imagine traveling back to the time of T. rex. You'd know you were in another era even if you never saw a dinosaur. Here are five big differences:

1. No flowers or grass. When dinosaurs first appeared, there were no flowering plants. Instead, you'd see ginkgo trees, horsetails, and cycads. Grass didn't exist yet!

2. It was hotter. The average global temperature was about 89°F (32°C), compared to about 59°F (15°C) today. The poles had no ice—just warm seawater.

3. One giant continent. Most land was joined together in a supercontinent called Pangaea. Over millions of years, it broke apart into the continents we know.

4. Different plants and animals. Early mammals were small but not all meek. Some ate dinosaurs! And the first birds were toothy.

5. No modern forests. The thick, leafy forests we have today only appeared after the asteroid strike 66 million years ago. That's when our primate ancestors evolved.

So next time you see a dinosaur movie, remember: the world itself was a totally different place.
why_it_matters: It helps you see that Earth itself changes over millions of years, so the plants and weather around you today will not always be the same.

background_read: T. rex (a huge meat-eating dinosaur with sharp teeth that lived at the end of the dinosaur age) walked through a world with no grass at all.
Pangaea (a name that means 'all the land') was the giant continent that later split into the continents we know today.
An asteroid (a huge rock from space) hit Earth about 66 million years ago, and many new kinds of forests and mammals spread afterward.
Article_Structure: WHO: You — imagining a trip back to the time of T. rex — plus the dinosaurs, early mammals, and first birds living then.
WHAT: Five big differences between the dinosaur world and our world today.
WHERE: On Earth long ago, mostly on the joined-up land of Pangaea, with warm seas and no ice at the poles.
WHY: To show that the whole planet — its plants, temperature, and land — was completely different, not just the animals.

perspectives.description: They love learning that the dinosaur world had strange trees like cycads and horsetails instead of grass and flowers.
They point out the hotter temperature and ice-free poles as an example of how a warmer Earth looks.
They might say dinosaur films look exciting but often forget how different the land and plants really were.
